Writer Go race-detector validation against sequential oracle
Independent bounded property and concurrency stress validation

claims.text: The source preserves a generic Go concurrency coding request, with goroutine synchronization or channel use as examples, but does not preserve a unique task API, ordering, concurrency degree or cancellation contract.

Under the declared square worker-pool reference exercise, the exact candidate preserves input order and matches the property oracle across bounded state-space and parallel stress runs under Go race detection.

validation.command: independent bounded property and concurrent stress under go test -race
validation.reported_stdout: PASS independent-small-state-space-depth=4 workers=1..7 invalid-workers=panic parallel-invocations=300 repeats=3 race-detector=pass timeout-deadlock-check=pass

boundary_tests.case: bounded exhaustive value sequences through depth 4 with workers 1..7
boundary_tests.expected: exact candidate equals independent sequential property oracle and every call returns before timeout
declared positive-worker reference contract rejects invalid worker counts by panic

boundary_tests.case: 300 parallel independent invocations repeated under race detector
boundary_tests.expected: all invocations equal oracle with no race or deadlock timeout

findings: The source preserves only a generic Go concurrency coding request and does not preserve one unique task contract; the candidate explicitly marks the square worker-pool as a reference exercise instead of source fact.

The worker/channel implementation has a coherent close protocol: producer closes jobs, workers drain and exit, coordinator waits for workers and only then closes results, collector ranges until results closes.
Workers do not share-write the output slice; one collector owns writes and restores source order by index, decoupling execution order from result order.
Independent bounded state-space checks, invalid-worker boundaries, and 300 parallel invocations repeated under the race detector match the property oracle without timeout/deadlock.

The answer distinguishes channel transport/backpressure from WaitGroup lifecycle synchronization and explicitly scopes cancellation/error propagation as follow-up requirements rather than preserved source constraints.
